$comment: presentations.get -> GET v1/presentations/{presentationId}, response Presentation. Read from Google's own discovery document 2026-10-01. The path the discovery document declares uses RFC 6570 reserved expansion ({+presentationId}) -- NOT adopted here. google-analytics is this estate's one deliberate {+var} user and a guard test refuses a second until the cross-runtime encoding gap it is pinned against is settled (RULES.md); a presentationId never contains a slash, so plain brace expansion is correct and sufficient. No scope change -- the presentations scope presentation_create already holds covers read too.
title: Google Slides presentation
description: Read a presentation's slides and the objectId of every element on them -- the prerequisite for targeting a specific shape or placeholder with a future edit.

config.label: Presentation ID
config.description: From presentation_create's data.presentationId, or the id in the presentation's own URL.

outputShape.description: One entry per slide, in order: objectId, and pageElements -- each with its own objectId and exactly one of shape/image/table/line/video/wordArt/sheetsChart/elementGroup/speakerSpotlight set, naming what kind of element it is. A placeholder shape's text (when it has one) lives at pageElements[].shape.text, published raw -- this connector does not flatten Slides' own rich-text run structure.
Which estate this ran against. Google has no sandbox, so: fake or live.
